item.title: Almost 25,000 premises in Kerry can now connect under National Broadband Plan
item.description: Almost 25,000 homes, farms and businesses in Kerry can now get high-speed fibre broadband under the National Broadband Plan. National Broadband Ireland is delivering minimum speeds of 500 megabits per second to premises across Kerry under the plan which will see investment of over €107 million into the county. item.title: TD Michael Cahill disqualified from driving for two years for dangerous driving
item.description: Kerry Fianna Fáil TD Michael Cahill was convicted of dangerous driving after a court heard he was driving at over 190kph on a motorway last March as a judge warned him “speed kills”. item.title: Palace manager to leave at end of season
item.description: Crystal Palace manager Oliver Glasner's announced that he will not be signing a new contract and will leave at the end of the season. The Austrian coach led the club to their first ever major trophy as they lifted the FA Cup in May. He says that he told Palace's chairman Steve Parish in October that he'd be moving on but now needed to make it official Advertisement Palace captain Marc Guehi is close to agreeing a move to Manchester City.

item.title: Derry sign McClean
item.description: Derry City have announced the signing of Patrick McClean from Sligo Rovers. The centre-back returns to the Brandywell on a two-year deal. He made 25 appearances across his first two stints with the Candystripes. Advertisement

item.title: Ireland suffer defeat in opening World Cup match
item.description: Ireland's under 19 Cricketers suffered defeat in their opening World Cup match in Namibia. Peter Johnston's side posted a target of 235 runs, which Australia chased down for the loss of two wickets. They'll return to action against Sri Lanka on Monday. Advertisement

Flu cases falling but rise in RSV and Covid means UHK is still under pressure
item.description: Flu cases presenting at UHK are starting to taper off, but rising incidence of RSV - as well as Covid - mean it'll be several weeks before pressure is eased on staff and services. That's according to Consultant in Emergency Medicine Dr Ronán Murphy, who says recent weeks have been challenging for staff at the Tralee hospital.
